expectations.text: Applies at least five named models
expectations.evidence: Lists all nine Vol. 1 models correctly and applies seven in depth (sections 1-7), plus the razors briefly in '8 & 9'. The names match SKILL.md.

expectations.text: Uses second-order thinking with concrete consequences
expectations.evidence: Section 5 table: 'Lose employer health insurance and 401(k) match... Harder to get a mortgage (lenders often want 2 years of self-employment history)', 'push local prices down by flooding your own market', 'career skills and network fade'.

expectations.text: Uses inversion (e.g. what would guarantee failure)
expectations.evidence: Section 7 'How to make sure this fails': 8 items ('Quit with less than 3 months of savings', 'Depend 100% on one platform'), each turned into a rule. This is generic; it has no Jacobi or force field, but it is correct inversion.

expectations.text: Uses circle of competence and/or probabilistic thinking with numbers
expectations.evidence: Probabilistic section with numbers: 'Bad case (say 30%)... Base case (say 50%)... Good case (say 20%)', plus fat tails and base rates. Circle of competence is applied correctly but generically (no Lifer/Stranger or the book's three steps).

expectations.text: Ends with a decision rule or test, not just a list
expectations.evidence: 'Putting It Together: A Decision Rule' - 'Quit when all of these are true' with 6 testable conditions (e.g. 3-6 months net profit >= 60-75% of take-home, 6-12 months runway) and a written exit ramp. The 'one-way/two-way door' framing is not presented as the book's.
